variants.title: The raccoon kits are waking up in the tree
variants.body: Mom's already halfway down the trunk. The kits follow one careful paw at a time, and somebody always slips the last bit.

variants.title: Raccoon family, coming down the tree
variants.body: First mom, then a wobbly line of kits. They wait at the bottom, sniffing the air, before heading out {place}.

variants.title: A raccoon is checking the trash cans
variants.body: Same route as last night: the can with the loose lid, then the one by the fence. Raccoons remember what worked.

variants.title: The night shift is making the rounds
variants.body: Somewhere {place}, a raccoon is feeling along the curb with those clever front paws, reading the block by touch.

variants.title: A raccoon is dabbling at a puddle
variants.body: Rolling a snack between wet paws. They aren't washing it: wet paws just feel things better.

variants.title: A raccoon is bulking up for winter
variants.body: Acorns, fallen fruit, a dropped slice of pizza. Everything counts this time of year.

variants.title: The raccoons are staying in tonight
variants.body: Too cold to bother. They're curled up in the den, tails over noses, waiting for a milder night.

variants.title: A raccoon peeks out, then thinks better of it
variants.body: On cold nights they'll skip a shift or two. The trash cans {place} can wait.

variants.title: A raccoon mom slips out for a quick bite
variants.body: Her kits are tucked in a den up high. She'll be back before they miss her.

variants.title: An opossum is tiptoeing along a fence
variants.body: Slow and steady, tail helping with balance. They're on bug and slug patrol {place}.

variants.title: An opossum is out snacking
variants.body: Fallen fruit, beetles, the odd snail. They clean up the block and ask for nothing.

variants.title: An opossum mom has passengers tonight
variants.body: A row of babies clings to her back, holding on tight while she waddles along.

variants.title: A young opossum is out on their own
variants.body: Everything is new: the curb, the hedge, the smell of the gardens {place}. They sniff it all.

variants.title: The opossums are keeping their ears warm
variants.body: Bare ears and tails don't like the cold. Tonight they're staying tucked in somewhere snug.

variants.title: Moths are circling the streetlight
variants.body: They steer by keeping the brightest light above them, so a streetlight sends them spinning. Every porch light switched off {place} helps.

variants.title: A little crowd at the lamp
variants.body: Fuzzy wings, feathery antennae, dizzy loops. Look closely: some are as patterned as butterflies.

variants.title: Moths are on the night shift at the flowers
variants.body: While the bees sleep, moths sip nectar and carry pollen from bloom to bloom.

variants.title: The last moths of the year are out
variants.body: On mild fall evenings a few still flutter by. Many will spend winter as cocoons tucked in fallen leaves.

variants.title: Pigeons are heading out for breakfast
variants.body: They leave the ledge in little groups and drop onto the sidewalk {place}, checking where crumbs landed last night.

variants.title: First flight of the morning
variants.body: A clap of wings, a loop around the block, and down they come to see what the day left out.

variants.title: A pigeon is sunbathing
variants.body: One wing tipped up, eyes half closed. The warmth shakes out parasites, and it just feels nice.

variants.title: A pigeon is showing off
variants.body: He puffs up, spins in a circle and bows, cooing the whole time. She keeps eating like she hasn't noticed.

variants.title: A pigeon is carrying a twig
variants.body: City pigeons nest any time of year. That twig is going to a ledge {place}, maybe one you walk under.

variants.title: Pigeons are huddled up
variants.body: Feathers fluffed into a down jacket, pressed together where the sun hits the building.

variants.title: The pigeons are back on the ledge
variants.body: Pairs settle in side by side. Same ledge, same partner, every night.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is awake
variants.body: The hedge {place} is chattering. That racket is how they keep track of who's where.

variants.title: Sparrows are taking a dust bath
variants.body: They wriggle into a dry patch of dirt and flick it through their feathers, like a dry shampoo.

variants.title: Sparrow kids are begging
variants.body: Fluffy youngsters chase their parents, wings fluttering, beaks wide open. The parents mostly give in.

variants.title: Sparrows are stuffing a gap with grass
variants.body: A sign, a traffic light, a hole in old brick: anywhere will do for a messy, cozy nest.

variants.title: The hedge is getting noisy
variants.body: Before bed, the whole gang gathers in the bushes and talks over the day. Loudly.

variants.title: The sparrows are tucked deep in the hedge
variants.body: Puffed into little round balls, shoulder to shoulder, out of the wind.

variants.title: A squirrel is burying an acorn
variants.body: Dig, drop, pat it down, look around to check who saw. If someone's watching, they might fake it and hide it somewhere else.

variants.title: Squirrels are planting next year's trees
variants.body: Every planter {place} is a pantry right now. The acorns they forget will sprout in spring.

variants.title: The squirrels are up and digging
variants.body: Morning is rush hour. They're checking old hiding spots and sniffing out breakfast {place}.

variants.title: Two squirrels are chasing around the tree
variants.body: Wild spirals up and down the trunk. It's courting season, and nobody's being subtle.

variants.title: A squirrel is splooting
variants.body: Flat on a cool branch, belly down, legs out. That's how a squirrel beats the heat.

variants.title: A squirrel mom is heading home to the drey
variants.body: Babies are tucked up in that ball of leaves. She checks on them between snack runs.

variants.title: A squirrel is heading up for the night
variants.body: Up the trunk to the drey, tail flicking. Bedtime comes early for squirrels.

variants.title: Starlings are lining up on the wire
variants.body: Dozens of them, chattering, before heading off together to a shared roost for the night.

variants.title: A starling is doing impressions
variants.body: Listen: a whistle, a click, maybe a car alarm. Starlings borrow sounds from {place} and mix them into their songs.

variants.title: Starlings are probing the lawn
variants.body: They stab their beaks into the grass and open them wide to pry up grubs. A clever little trick.

variants.title: A starling is singing from a chimney
variants.body: All dressed up in glossy purple and green, wings flicking, putting on a show.

variants.title: Young starlings are following their parents
variants.body: Plain brown and very loud, they trail the grown-ups across the grass begging for bugs.

variants.title: Starlings are wearing their stars
variants.body: Their winter feathers are covered in white speckles. Catch one in the sun and it sparkles.

variants.title: A mourning dove is cooing
variants.body: That soft, slow hoo-OO-oo-oo isn't sad at all. It's a love song from a wire {place}.

variants.title: Two doves are sitting close
variants.body: Side by side on the wire, preening each other. Mourning doves usually come in pairs.

variants.title: A dove is building the world's simplest nest
variants.body: A few twigs on a fire escape. Somehow, it's enough.

variants.title: Mourning doves are picking at seeds
variants.body: A small group walks the ground, bobbing their heads. When they take off, listen for the whistle of their wings.

variants.title: The doves are soaking up the last sun
variants.body: Puffed up on the wire, facing the sunset, catching every bit of warmth before night.

variants.title: A robin is starting the dawn chorus
variants.body: Before the sun is up, one robin sings, then another. Listen for a cheery, rolling song {place}.

variants.title: A robin is hunting worms
variants.body: Run, stop, tilt the head, pounce. That tilt isn't listening: they look at the ground with one eye.

variants.title: A robin fledgling is learning the ropes
variants.body: Spotty chest, stubby tail, lots of hopping. A parent is nearby with a worm. No rescue needed.

variants.title: Robins are raiding the berries
variants.body: Worms are getting scarce, so they've switched to fruit. A group can strip a tree in an afternoon.

variants.title: A robin is singing the day out
variants.body: First to sing in the morning and among the last at night.

variants.title: A quiet flock of robins is passing through
variants.body: Plenty of robins stay all winter. They stop singing and travel in groups, looking for berries.

variants.title: A gull is riding the wind
variants.body: Wings barely moving, drifting over {place} like it's no effort at all. It mostly isn't.

variants.title: A gull is cracking a clam
variants.body: Up, up, then drop it on the rocks. If it doesn't break, they'll try again. And again.

variants.title: A gull is perched on a piling
variants.body: Watching the water {place}, waiting to see what the morning tide brings in.

variants.title: Gulls are heading out to the water for the night
variants.body: They sleep floating together on the harbor, safe from anything on land.

variants.title: A gull is guarding a rooftop nest
variants.body: Gulls nest on flat roofs around the city. Get too close and you'll hear about it.

variants.title: A young gull is whining for lunch
variants.body: Mottled brown and as big as the grown-ups, still begging. The red spot on a parent's beak is the doorbell.

variants.title: A monarch is drinking from the flowers
variants.body: Wings opening and closing slowly in the sun. Every sip is fuel.

variants.title: A monarch is flying south
variants.body: This butterfly is headed to the mountains of Mexico, a place they've never been, by way of {place}.

variants.title: A monarch is laying eggs on milkweed
variants.body: One tiny egg per leaf. Milkweed is the only plant their caterpillars can eat.

variants.title: Monarchs are settling in for the night
variants.body: Travelers rest together on branches, wings folded, before tomorrow's leg of the trip.

variants.title: A red-tailed hawk is sitting very still
variants.body: Up on a ledge {place}, watching the ground below. They can wait an hour for one good chance.

variants.title: A hawk is circling overhead
variants.body: Wide, lazy loops on rising warm air. Look for the rusty red tail when they bank.

variants.title: Two red-tails are courting
variants.body: Soaring together in big circles. Sometimes one dives and they touch talons in the air.

variants.title: A red-tail is sitting on eggs
variants.body: In a big stick nest on a building or a tall tree. Their mate brings dinner.

variants.title: A young hawk is screaming for dinner
variants.body: That long wheeze is a fledgling asking the parents to hurry up while they learn to hunt.

variants.title: A hawk is tucking in for the night
variants.body: Perched close to a tree trunk, out of the wind, done for the day.

variants.title: A blue jay is hiding acorns
variants.body: They can carry several at once in their throat. The ones they forget grow into oaks {place}.

variants.title: A blue jay is pretending to be a hawk
variants.body: That hawk scream might be a jay. Maybe it clears everyone off the good branch. Maybe it's just fun.

variants.title: A blue jay is announcing the morning
variants.body: JAY! JAY! Bright blue against bare branches, and loud about it.

variants.title: A blue jay is being sneaky
variants.body: Near their nest, the loudest bird on the block slips in and out without a sound.

variants.title: A blue jay family is on the move
variants.body: The youngsters follow the grown-ups through the trees and copy everything they do.

variants.title: Juncos are hopping under the hedge
variants.body: Little gray birds with snowy bellies, scratching for seeds. When they fly, their tails flash white.

variants.title: The first juncos just landed
variants.body: They flew down from Canada overnight and touched down {place}. They'll stay till spring.

variants.title: A junco is trilling before the trip north
variants.body: A quick, bright trill from a branch. In a few weeks they'll be gone till fall.

variants.title: Juncos are tucking into the hedge for the night
variants.body: A small flock huddles low in the bushes, out of the wind.

variants.title: Crows are commuting home
variants.body: Long lines of them cross the sky at dusk, all heading to the same few roosts to sleep together.

variants.title: The crows are fanning out for the day
variants.body: Thousands slept together last night. Now each family heads back to their own patch, maybe {place}.

variants.title: A crow is keeping an eye on things
variants.body: Crows remember faces. Be friendly and you might get a nod back.

variants.title: A crow family is feeding the new chicks
variants.body: Last year's kids help out. Big sisters and brothers bring food to the nest.

variants.title: Young crows are begging loudly
variants.body: Fluffy, noisy and following the parents everywhere. Patience is not a crow-kid skill.

variants.title: A White-throated Sparrow is whistling
variants.body: Oh sweet Canada, Canada, Canada. A thin, clear song from the bushes {place}.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are scratching in the leaves
variants.body: Both feet at once, hop-kick backward. They're finding bugs and seeds under the leaf litter.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are back
variants.body: They flew in from Canadian forests and will spend the winter in the bushes here.

variants.title: White-throated Sparrows are fueling up
variants.body: In a few weeks they'll head north. Right now it's all snacks and practice songs.

variants.title: Chimney swifts are zipping overhead
variants.body: Tiny cigar-shaped birds, twittering, catching bugs on the wing. They hardly ever land.

variants.title: Swifts are swirling down a chimney
variants.body: As the light goes, they circle and pour into an old chimney {place} to roost, clinging to the inside wall.

variants.title: The chimney swifts are back
variants.body: Fresh in from South America. Listen for high twittering over the rooftops.

variants.title: The pigeons are asleep on the ledge
variants.body: Heads tucked into their back feathers, pressed together in pairs, a few floors above the sidewalk {place}.

variants.title: A pigeon is dozing under the eaves
variants.body: One foot up, feathers fluffed. City noise doesn't bother them a bit.

variants.title: The sparrow gang is asleep in the hedge
variants.body: Deep inside the bushes, all puffed up together. The chatter starts again at first light.

variants.title: A squirrel is curled up in the drey
variants.body: Wrapped in their own tail like a blanket, high in a ball of leaves. In winter, sometimes two share for warmth.

variants.title: The crows are sleeping in a giant roost
variants.body: Hundreds, sometimes thousands, packed into the same stand of trees. There's safety in numbers.

variants.title: The gulls are asleep on the water
variants.body: Floating together out on the harbor, bobbing with the waves, safe from anything on land.

variants.title: The juncos are asleep low in the hedge
variants.body: Tucked close to the ground, out of the wind, saving every bit of warmth for tomorrow.

variants.title: The robins are roosting in the trees
variants.body: Dads and young robins often sleep together in a big group roost, then scatter at dawn.
